questions.question: Gadgil formula is concerned with:

options.text: distribution of Central Assistance among the state
distribution of natural resources to the states

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**distribution of Central Assistance among the states**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gadgil Formula** was formulated in **1969** for the allocation of **Central Assistance** to states for development purposes.
 
• The formula aimed to ensure an equitable distribution of resources among states, focusing on the **developmental needs of economically weaker and backward regions.**
 
• It divided Central Assistance based on **criteria such as population, per capita income, tax effort, and special problems faced by states.**
 
• The formula was revised multiple times, including during the **Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002),** to accommodate changing socio-economic conditions.
 
• The primary objective of the formula was to promote **balanced economic development** across various states in India. *Hence, the correct answer is distribution of Central Assistance among the states.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of Gadgil Formula:**

 
 
• Introduced during the **Fourth Five-Year Plan (**1969-1974**)** to ensure equitable resource allocation among states.
 
• Initially, it allocated **60% of funds** based on population, **25% on per capita income**, and the remaining **15% on factors such as tax effort and special problems.**
 
 
 
• **Revisions:**
 
 
• Revised during the **Ninth Five-Year Plan** with increased focus on **poverty reduction and backwardness.**
 
• Modifications included greater weightage for states with lower per capita income and special considerations for hilly and tribal areas.
 
 
 
• **Application:**
 
 
• Used as a guiding framework for allocating **Plan Assistance** until replaced by the Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula in **1991.**
 
• Continued to influence government policies aimed at **balanced regional development.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Criteria for Allocation:**

 
 
• Population: Larger states received higher allocations due to their higher population size.
 
• Per Capita Income: States with lower per capita income were prioritized for greater assistance.
 
• Tax Effort: States demonstrating higher revenue mobilization were incentivized.
 
• Special Problems: Specific challenges faced by certain states, such as natural disasters, were considered.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• Promoted **regional equity** and balanced economic development across states.
 
• Helped address disparities between **developed and underdeveloped regions** in India.

questions.question: To which of the following Indian states does Mohiniattam classical dance form belong?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohiniattam** is one of the eight recognized classical dance forms of India.
 
• It originated in the state of **Kerala** and has deep roots in the region's culture, traditions, and art.
 
• The term "Mohiniattam" is derived from the word "Mohini," which refers to a divine enchantress in Hindu mythology, and "attam," which means dance.
 
• This dance form is characterized by its graceful movements, subtle expressions, and storytelling elements that are inspired by Hindu mythology and Kerala's rich cultural heritage.
 
• The dance uses a unique costume style, primarily featuring a white sari with gold borders, known as the "Kasavu" sari, which is traditional to Kerala.
 
• Mohiniattam is performed as a solo recital and is traditionally performed by women.
 
• The music accompanying Mohiniattam is based on the **Sopana** style of music, which is native to Kerala.
 
• The themes of Mohiniattam performances often revolve around love, devotion, and the divine, with many stories being inspired by Hindu epics like the **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Characteristics of Mohiniattam:**

 
 
• Mohiniattam is known for its **graceful, feminine movements** and involves circular and swaying motions that resemble the gentle waves of Kerala's backwaters.
 
• The hand gestures or "mudras" play a vital role in Mohiniattam, helping the dancer narrate intricate stories.
 
• The dance is performed at a slow pace and emphasizes expressions or "abhinaya," making it highly emotive.
 
• **Musical accompaniment** typically includes instruments like the **mridangam, veena, edakka**, and flute.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dance Forms of India:**
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam:** Originating from Tamil Nadu, Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms.
 
• **Kathak:** This dance form originates from northern India and is known for its intricate footwork and spins.
 
• **Odissi:** A classical dance form from Odisha, characterized by fluid movements and sculpturesque poses.
 
• **Kuchipudi:** Originating from Andhra Pradesh, this dance form blends drama and dance.
 
• **Manipuri:** This dance form comes from Manipur and is known for its graceful and lyrical nature.
 
• **Kathakali:** Another classical dance form from Kerala, Kathakali is characterized by elaborate costumes and makeup.
 
• **Sattriya:** Originating from Assam, it is performed in monasteries and has deep roots in Vaishnavism.
 
 
 
• **Important Points about Kerala:**
 
 
• Kerala is located in the southern part of India and is known as "God's Own Country" for its natural beauty.
 
• The state has a rich tradition of art forms, including dance, music, and literature.
 
• Kerala is famous for its backwaters, spices, and temples, which influence its cultural heritage.

questions.question: Select the correct sequence of materials put one after the other as per the order of element, compound, and homogeneous mixture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Elements:** Elements are pure substances that consist of only one type of atom. Examples include **iron**, **mercury**, and other metals. These cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.
 
• **Compounds:** Compounds are pure substances composed of two or more elements chemically combined in fixed proportions. For instance, **methane (CH4)** is a compound consisting of carbon and hydrogen atoms.
 
• **Homogeneous mixtures:** Homogeneous mixtures are mixtures in which the composition is uniform throughout. For example, **sea water** is a homogeneous mixture containing dissolved salts and other minerals uniformly distributed in water.
 
• The sequence in **Option 2**—**Iron** (element), **Methane** (compound), and **Sea Water** (homogeneous mixture)—correctly follows the order of *element, compound, and homogeneous mixture*. *Hence, Option 2 is correct.*
 
• Other options do not follow the correct order of classification, as some mix elements, compounds, and heterogeneous mixtures or do not provide the proper sequence. *Hence, other options are incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Elements:**

 
 
• Elements are fundamental substances that cannot be broken down further. Examples include **gold, oxygen, and hydrogen**.
 
• Elements are classified as metals, non-metals, and metalloids based on their properties.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Compounds:**
 
 
• Compounds are formed by the chemical combination of two or more elements in fixed ratios. Examples include **water (H2O)** and **carbon dioxide (CO2)**.
 
• Compounds have properties different from their constituent elements. For instance, water (H2O) is liquid, while hydrogen and oxygen are gases.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Homogeneous Mixtures:**
 
 
• Homogeneous mixtures have a uniform composition throughout. Examples include **air** and **sea water**.
 
• They can be separated into their components by physical methods, such as evaporation or distillation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Mixtures:**

 
 
• Homogeneous mixtures have a uniform composition throughout (e.g., air, saltwater), while heterogeneous mixtures have non-uniform composition (e.g., sand and water).
 
• Homogeneous mixtures are also known as solutions, while heterogeneous mixtures are mixtures with distinguishable components.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• **Elements:** Used in industries for making tools, machinery, and construction materials.
 
• **Compounds:** Widely used in pharmaceuticals, agriculture, and chemical industries.
 
• **Homogeneous Mixtures:** Used in everyday life, such as saline solutions in medical treatments and beverages.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Abhinav Bharat Mandir (Young India Society)?

options.text: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and Ganesh Damodar Savarkar

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and Ganesh Damodar Savarkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abhinav Bharat Mandir**, also known as the **Young India Society**, was founded by **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar** and his brother **Ganesh Damodar Savarkar** in **1904**.
 
• The organization aimed to promote revolutionary activities against British colonial rule in India and worked to inspire Indian youth to fight for independence.
 
• Abhinav Bharat Mandir was initially started as a secret society in **Nashik**, Maharashtra, and later expanded its influence across India. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar**, also known as **Veer Savarkar**, was a prominent revolutionary, writer, and nationalist who played a significant role in India's freedom struggle.
 
• The society organized several revolutionary activities, including armed resistance against British rule, and inspired individuals to engage in acts of patriotism. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• It was disbanded later by the British authorities due to its involvement in revolutionary activities. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and Ganesh Damodar Savarkar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar:**

 
 
• **Born:** 28 May 1883 in Nashik, Maharashtra, Savarkar was an influential revolutionary, writer, and nationalist leader.
 
• He advocated for armed resistance against British rule and inspired the youth to participate in the Indian independence movement.
 
• Savarkar also coined the term **Hindutva** and emphasized cultural and religious nationalism.
 
 
 
• **Ganesh Damodar Savarkar:**
 
 
• **Brother of Vinayak Savarkar:** Ganesh Damodar Savarkar was also actively involved in revolutionary activities and contributed to the formation of the Abhinav Bharat Mandir.
 
• He played a key role in organizing revolutionary actions and inspiring patriotism among Indian youth.
 
 
 
• **Abhinav Bharat Mandir:**
 
 
• The organization was secretive and aimed at mobilizing Indians to revolt against British colonial rule.
 
• It encouraged armed resistance and revolutionary activities to achieve independence.
 
• The British authorities disbanded the organization due to its involvement in revolutionary acts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Abhinav Bharat Mandir:**

 
 
• The society played a significant role in shaping revolutionary activities and inspiring patriotism among Indian youth.
 
• **Key Members:** Apart from the Savarkar brothers, the organization attracted numerous revolutionary leaders who contributed to India's independence struggle.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• The efforts of Abhinav Bharat Mandir are remembered as a stepping stone in the Indian independence movement.
 
• The ideals and sacrifices of its members continue to inspire future generations in India.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, what was the child sex ratio of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**919**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As per the **Census 2011**, the **child sex ratio** in India was reported to be **919 females per 1000 males** in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• The **child sex ratio** is an important demographic indicator that reflects the number of girls per 1000 boys in a specific age group, typically under the age of 6 years.
 
• The declining child sex ratio has been a matter of concern for policymakers and society, as it indicates a preference for male children and the prevalence of **sex-selective practices.**
 
• The child sex ratio in India has been steadily declining since the 1960s. The 2011 Census showed a further decline from the 2001 Census, where the ratio was recorded as **927 females per 1000 males**.
 
• This decline is attributed to factors like **female feticide, gender-based discrimination, and societal preference for male children**.
 
• The government has introduced several schemes and laws, such as the **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act** of 1994, to curb sex-selective abortions and improve the child sex ratio in India.
 
• The **Betti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)** scheme launched in 2015 aims to address the declining child sex ratio and promote the education of girl children.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 919.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):**

 
 
• The **child sex ratio** is defined as the number of girls per 1000 boys in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• It is an important indicator of the **social health of a society** and reflects the extent of gender discrimination and practices such as sex-selective abortions.
 
 
 
• **Trends in Child Sex Ratio:**
 
 
• In **India**, the child sex ratio has been declining over the years. It was **945 in 1991**, **927 in 2001**, and further decreased to **919 in 2011**.
 
• This decline highlights the prevalence of gender-based discrimination and social biases in favor of male children.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Improve CSR:**
 
 
• The **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act**, 1994, prohibits sex determination of the fetus to curb female feticide.
 
• The **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)** scheme, launched in 2015, aims to address declining child sex ratios and promote awareness about the importance of girl children.
 
• Various state-level initiatives, such as the **Laadli Scheme** in Haryana, provide financial incentives to families for educating and supporting girl children.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impacts of Declining Child Sex Ratio:**

 
 
• A declining child sex ratio leads to long-term social and demographic challenges, such as an imbalanced population structure and increased gender-based violence.
 
• It reflects a deep-rooted societal preference for sons over daughters, which can hinder overall progress in achieving gender equality.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective:**
 
 
• Globally, countries like **China** also face similar issues due to their **one-child policy**, which resulted in a skewed sex ratio.
 
• Efforts at the global level, such as **UNICEF campaigns**, focus on promoting gender equality and reducing gender-based discrimination.

questions.question: Which Iranian-origin group was known in Indian sources as Shaka-Pahlava?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Parthians**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shaka-Pahlava** mentioned in Indian sources refers to two groups: the **Shakas** (Scythians) and the **Pahlavas** (Parthians). These groups were of **Iranian origin** and migrated to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• The **Parthians** were a significant ancient Iranian-origin group who entered India around the 1st century CE. They are known to have ruled parts of northwestern India and Afghanistan.
 
• The term “Pahlava” in Indian texts often refers to the Parthians, who were known for their interaction with the Indian kingdoms, including the Satavahanas. *Hence, the correct answer is Parthians.*
 
• The Parthians ruled simultaneously with other groups of foreign origin like the **Shakas** and **Kushanas**. Their cultural and political influence extended to the regions of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Indian sources such as the **Puranas** and epigraphs mention the Shaka-Pahlava as Iranian-origin rulers who played a role in shaping the early medieval history of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indo-Greeks:**

 
 
• The Indo-Greeks, also known as **Yavanas**, were descendants of the Greeks who ruled parts of northwest India and Afghanistan after Alexander the Great’s invasion in **326 BCE**.
 
• They are famous for their cultural contributions, especially in art and architecture, and their role in spreading **Hellenistic culture** in India.
 
 
 
• **Shakas:**
 
 
• The Shakas, or Scythians, were another group of **Iranian origin** who migrated to India in the 2nd century BCE.
 
• They established several kingdoms in western India, including Gujarat and Rajasthan, and were known for their interaction with Indian dynasties like the Satavahanas.
 
• **Example:** The famous Shaka king **Rudradaman** is known for his inscription at Junagadh in Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **Kushanas:**
 
 
• The Kushanas were a Central Asian dynasty who ruled parts of India, Central Asia, and China during the 1st century CE.
 
• Their most famous ruler, **Kanishka**, played a significant role in the spread of **Buddhism** and contributed to the development of the Gandhara art style.
 
• The Kushanas were known for their extensive trade networks and cultural exchange across Asia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Significance of Shaka-Pahlava:**

 
 
• The Shaka-Pahlava period in Indian history is notable for the influx of foreign-origin rulers who contributed to the cultural and political landscape of India.
 
• These groups played a role in the development of art, architecture, and trade during their reign in India.
 
 
 
• **Interactions with Indian Kingdoms:**
 
 
• The Shaka-Pahlava rulers interacted with Indian dynasties such as the Mauryas, Satavahanas, and Guptas, leading to cultural synthesis.
 
• They are often mentioned in Indian texts like the Puranas and epigraphic records, which highlight their contributions to Indian history.
 
• Their rule marked a period of significant cultural and political changes in ancient India.

questions.question: In which year was Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana launched by the government of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2020**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana (ABRY)** was launched by the **Government of India** on **October 1, 2020**.
 
• This scheme was introduced as part of the **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan** (Self-Reliant India Movement), which aimed to boost economic growth and self-reliance amid the challenges posed by the **COVID-19 pandemic**.
 
• The primary objective of the ABRY is to incentivize employers to create new jobs and provide **social security benefits** to a larger section of the workforce.
 
• Under this scheme, the government provides **financial support** to employers for hiring new employees. It contributes to both the **employee's and employer's share of EPF (Employees’ Provident Fund) contributions** for newly recruited employees for a specific period.
 
• The scheme aims to reduce the financial burden on employers and encourage them to recruit more workers, thereby addressing the unemployment crisis caused by the pandemic.
 
• It was specifically targeted at employees earning a monthly wage of less than **₹15,000** and who were not working in any establishment registered with the **Employees’ Provident Fund Organization (EPFO)** before **October 1, 2020**.
 
• The scheme also aimed to cover those workers who had lost their jobs between **March 1, 2020, and September 30, 2020**, due to the pandemic and were able to secure employment on or after October 1, 2020.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan:**

 
 
• The Aatmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan or **Self-Reliant India Campaign** was announced by the Government of India in May 2020 to revive the Indian economy post-COVID-19 and make the country self-reliant.
 
• The campaign focuses on key pillars such as **economy, infrastructure, technology, demography, and demand**.
 
 
 
• **Features of Aatmanirbhar Bharat Rojgar Yojana:**
 
 
• The government contributes **24% of the wages** (12% employer share + 12% employee share) for establishments employing up to **1,000 employees**.
 
• For establishments employing more than **1,000 employees**, the government contributes **12% of employees’ wages**.
 
• The benefits are available for a period of **two years** from the date of employment.
 
• The benefits under the scheme are available for employees who are registered with **EPFO** and hold an **Aadhaar-seeded Universal Account Number (UAN)**.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility Criteria:**
 
 
• Employees earning less than **₹15,000** per month are eligible for this scheme.
 
• The employee must not have been working in any establishment registered with **EPFO** before **October 1, 2020**.
 
• Workers who lost their jobs between **March 1, 2020, and September 30, 2020**, and secured employment on or after October 1, 2020, are also eligible.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of ABRY:**

 
 
• This scheme was a crucial step in addressing the **unemployment crisis** caused by the pandemic by incentivizing employers to hire more workers.
 
• It ensured **social security benefits** for a larger section of the workforce by extending EPF contributions to new employees.
 
• The scheme was also significant in creating a formal workforce and enhancing compliance with labor laws.
 
 
 
• **Other Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **PM Garib Kalyan Yojana** also aimed to address unemployment and economic challenges during the pandemic by providing financial support to the vulnerable sections of society.
 
• **MGNREGA** (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) also played a significant role in providing employment opportunities during the pandemic, especially in rural areas.

questions.question: Which Five-Year Plan aimed at making India self-reliant and focused on 'Defense and Development' due to external aggression and economic constraints?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Third Five-Year Plan** (1961–1966) was launched with the aim of achieving **self-reliance** and focusing on **economic stability**.
 
• The plan emphasized **agriculture** as its primary sector to ensure sufficient food production and reduce dependency on imports.
 
• Due to external aggression, particularly the **Indo-China War (1962)**, the plan shifted focus toward **‘Defense and Development’** to strengthen national security and economic growth. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The plan faced significant challenges due to the war and required adjustments in its objectives. The resources initially allocated for development were redirected toward **defense expenditure.**
 
• This Five-Year Plan also introduced measures to improve **industrial output** and infrastructure while addressing the constraints posed by the war.
 
• The Third Plan was affected by **economic constraints**, including a shortage of resources and inflation, which hindered achieving some of its goals.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Third Plan.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Five-Year Plans of India:**

 
 
• India adopted the strategy of planned development post-independence, starting with the **First Five-Year Plan** in **1951**, which focused on agriculture and rural development.
 
• Each plan aimed to address specific socio-economic challenges and set goals for the country’s development in sectors like agriculture, industry, education, and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Details of Other Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• **First Plan (1951–1956):** Focused on agriculture and irrigation.
 
• **Second Plan (1956–1961):** Emphasized industrialization with the development of heavy industries.
 
• **Fourth Plan (1969–1974):** Focused on growth with stability and self-reliance.
 
• **Sixth Plan (1980–1985):** Focused on poverty eradication and employment generation.
 
• **Seventh Plan (1985–1990):** Concentrated on productivity, technology, and efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Indo-China War on the Third Plan:**
 
 
• The **1962 Indo-China War** disrupted the economic focus of the Third Plan and necessitated a shift toward defense spending.
 
• This led to a decline in funds available for planned development and economic activities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Third Plan was initiated during a period of significant international tension, including the **Cold War** and regional conflicts.
 
• It was the first plan to emphasize **self-reliance**, considering the geopolitical and economic constraints of the time.
 
 
 
• **Achievements and Challenges:**
 
 
• The Third Plan achieved progress in areas like agriculture and industrial production despite challenges.
 
• However, the focus on defense due to the war limited its overall success in achieving long-term developmental goals.

questions.question: According to the Constitution of India, what is the maximum tenure of the election commissioner of India?

• **Tenure of Election Commissioner:** According to the Indian Constitution, the tenure of the **Election Commissioner of India** is limited to a period of **six years** or until the age of **65 years**, whichever comes earlier. This provision ensures a balance between experience and efficiency.
 
• The Election Commissioner is responsible for conducting free and fair elections for the **Parliament, State Legislatures, and offices of the President and Vice President.**
 
• **Article 324:** The **Election Commission** is established under **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution. It governs the entire process of elections in India, including their supervision, direction, and control.
 
• The tenure is designed to ensure that the Election Commissioner has sufficient time to contribute effectively to the electoral process, while also ensuring that there is a limit on the duration of service. *Hence, six years is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Election Commission of India:**

 
 
• The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is an independent constitutional authority responsible for administering elections in India.
 
• Established in **1950**, the commission ensures free and fair elections for the **Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislatures, and the offices of the President and Vice-President.**
 
 
 
• **Composition of ECI:**
 
 
• Initially, the ECI consisted of a **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC).**
 
• Later, it was expanded to include **two additional Election Commissioners** in **1993**, making it a multi-member body.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility and Conditions:**
 
 
• **Age:** The Election Commissioners must retire at the age of **65 years**.
 
• **Appointment:** The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.
 
• **Removal:** The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office only through a process similar to the removal of a Supreme Court judge, ensuring independence.
 
 
 
• **Functions of ECI:**
 
 
• Conduct elections for various constitutional positions.
 
• Supervise political parties and ensure their compliance with election rules.
 
• Handle disputes related to elections and the recognition of political parties.

• **Legal Framework:**

 
 
• The Election Commission operates under the provisions of the **Representation of the People Act, 1951** and other relevant laws.
 
• It ensures compliance with election guidelines and resolves electoral disputes.
 
 
 
• **Reforms:**
 
 
• Over the years, the Election Commission has introduced reforms such as **electronic voting machines (EVMs)**, voter identity cards, and transparency in political funding.

questions.question: Saroja Vaidyanathan, the recipient of Padma Shri in 2002 and Padma Bhushan in 2013 is a dancer of which classical dance form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saroja Vaidyanathan** is a renowned **Bharatanatyam dancer** from India. Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest and most celebrated classical dance forms originating in Tamil Nadu.
 
• She is a recipient of prestigious awards like the **Padma Shri (2002)** and **Padma Bhushan (2013)**, which are among the highest civilian honors in India, recognizing her immense contribution to dance and arts.
 
• Bharatanatyam is characterized by its intricate footwork, graceful movements, and emotive expressions (known as **abhinaya**). It combines elements of **music, rhythm, and storytelling**, making it a holistic art form.
 
• Saroja Vaidyanathan has trained numerous students and contributed extensively to the preservation and global promotion of Bharatanatyam. Her work has strengthened the cultural heritage of India. *Hence, Bharatanatyam is the correct answer.*
 
• **Other dance forms mentioned in the options**, like Manipuri, Odissi, and Kathak, are also classical dance forms of India but are distinct in their regional origins, techniques, and styles. These are not associated with Saroja Vaidyanathan. *Hence, Bharatanatyam is the correct answer.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• **Bharatanatyam** originated in Tamil Nadu and is considered one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, dating back over 2,000 years.
 
• It is deeply rooted in **Hindu mythology and temple traditions**, primarily performed as a form of devotion to deities.
 
• The term Bharatanatyam is derived from **Bha** (Bhava - expression), **Ra** (Raga - melody), **Ta** (Tala - rhythm), and **Natyam** (dance).
 
• It is known for its rigorous techniques, including **adavus** (basic steps), intricate footwork, symmetrical body postures, and graceful gestures known as **mudras**.
 
 
 
• **Other Dance Forms:**
 
 
• **Manipuri:** Originates in Manipur and is known for its graceful and soft movements. It is typically performed during religious ceremonies and narrates stories of **Radha-Krishna.**
 
• **Odissi:** Originates in Odisha and is characterized by fluid movements and sculpturesque poses. It is deeply spiritual, often based on themes from Hindu scriptures like **Jayadeva's Gita Govinda.**
 
• **Kathak:** Originates in Northern India and is known for its intricate footwork, spins, and storytelling through dance. It is performed both in **temples and courts** and incorporates influences from Persian culture.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards:**
 
 
• **Padma Shri:** The fourth highest civilian award in India, given for distinguished contributions in various fields.
 
• **Padma Bhushan:** The third highest civilian award in India, recognizing exceptional service in arts, literature, science, and public affairs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Significance:**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam has evolved from temple rituals to modern stage performances, preserving its spiritual and cultural essence.
 
• It is often performed solo and involves elaborate costumes, traditional makeup, and ornaments, enhancing the visual appeal.
 
 
 
• **Saroja Vaidyanathan's Contribution:**
 
 
• She has authored several books on Bharatanatyam and established dance academies to train future generations.
 
• Her efforts have significantly contributed to the global recognition and appreciation of Bharatanatyam as a classical art form.

questions.question: The Indian Financial System Code (IFSC) is a/an ________ character code for identifying the bank and branch in which an account is held.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eleven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Financial System Code (IFSC)** is an alphanumeric code of **11 characters** assigned to every bank branch by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
 
• This code is used to identify the bank and its branch uniquely during electronic payment systems like **NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer), RTGS (Real-Time Gross Settlement), and IMPS (Immediate Payment Service).**
 
• The structure of the IFSC code consists of:
 
 
• The first four characters represent the bank name (e.g., **SBIN for State Bank of India**).
 
• The fifth character is always **zero (0)**, reserved for future use.
 
• The last six characters denote the specific branch code of the bank.
 
 
 
• IFSC plays a crucial role in facilitating secure and accurate transactions across banking systems in **India**.
 
• For example, an IFSC code for a branch of **State Bank of India** in Delhi could be **SBIN0001234**, where **SBIN** identifies the bank, **0** is a reserved character, and **001234** indicates the branch.
 
• The IFSC code is mandatory for electronic payment systems, ensuring that funds are accurately transferred to the intended recipient and minimizing errors or misdirection.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Eleven.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Use of IFSC Code:**

 
 
• IFSC is essential for the **smooth functioning of electronic payment systems**, such as NEFT, RTGS, and IMPS, which are widely used in India for transferring money.
 
• It ensures that transactions are routed to the correct bank and branch, minimizing errors and delays.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Online Transactions:**
 
 
• The IFSC code is used for **online banking activities**, including the payment of bills, transfer of funds, and transactions related to e-commerce platforms.
 
• It facilitates the identification of the exact branch of a bank, ensuring accuracy in financial transactions.
 
 
 
• **Structure of IFSC Code:**
 
 
• The **first four characters** represent the bank name, providing clarity about the financial institution involved in the transaction.
 
• The **fifth character** is reserved as zero, which can be used for expansion or future purposes.
 
• The **last six characters** identify the branch uniquely, ensuring that the payment reaches the correct destination.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Authority:**
 
 
• The IFSC code is assigned and regulated by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, India’s central banking authority.
 
• The RBI ensures that every bank and branch has a unique IFSC code for transparency and efficiency in financial transactions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Functions of IFSC Code:**

 
 
• It helps in distinguishing different branches of the same bank, which is crucial in a vast country like **India** with numerous banks and branches.
 
• It ensures the accuracy and security of electronic fund transfers, reducing the risk of fraud or errors.
 
 
 
• **Examples of IFSC Usage:**
 
 
• When initiating a **NEFT** transaction, the sender must input the beneficiary’s IFSC code to ensure the funds are directed to the correct branch.
 
• Similarly, for paying utility bills or e-commerce transactions, the IFSC code is required for bank verification.

questions.question: What is the concept of ecological niche?

options.text: Ecological niche refers to a species' specific role in an ecosystem.
Ecological niche refers to the genetic diversity within a species.
Ecological niche is solely determined by an organism's habitat.
Ecological niche refers to the physical space a species occupies.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ecological niche refers to a species' specific role in an ecosystem**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Definition of Ecological Niche:** An ecological niche refers to the specific role or function of a species within an ecosystem. It encompasses how the species interacts with the environment, including its use of resources and interactions with other organisms.
 
• **Characteristics of an Ecological Niche:** It involves the species’ behavior, dietary habits, habitat use, reproduction, and the role it plays in energy flow and nutrient cycling within the ecosystem.
 
• **Correctness of Statement 1:** The statement accurately defines an ecological niche, emphasizing the species' unique role in the ecosystem. Hence, *statement 1 is correct.*
 
• **Statement 2:** Ecological niche does not refer to genetic diversity within a species. Genetic diversity is a separate concept related to variation in genes among individuals of a species. Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• **Statement 3:** Ecological niche is not solely determined by an organism's habitat. While habitat is a part of the niche, the niche also includes behaviors, interactions, and resource utilization. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• **Statement 4:** Ecological niche refers to more than just the physical space a species occupies. It includes ecological functions and interactions. Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of Ecological Niche:**

 
 
• **Habitat:** The specific physical location where a species lives. For instance, frogs live in wet habitats like ponds and marshes.
 
• **Dietary Habits:** Includes the food sources a species depends on. For example, herbivores like deer feed on plants, while carnivores like lions hunt other animals.
 
• **Behavioral Patterns:** Includes activities like mating rituals, migration, and predation strategies.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Ecological Niches:**
 
 
• **Polar Bear:** Occupies an arctic niche, feeding primarily on seals, adapted to cold environments, and plays a role as a top predator in its ecosystem.
 
• **Bees:** Serve as pollinators, contributing to plant reproduction and maintaining biodiversity.
 
• **Sea Otters:** Maintain kelp forest ecosystems by controlling sea urchin populations.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ecological Niche:**
 
 
• Understanding niches helps in conserving biodiversity by identifying critical roles species play in ecosystems.
 
• It aids in ecological modeling and predicting how ecosystems respond to changes like climate change or species extinction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference between Ecological Niche and Habitat:**

 
 
• **Habitat:** Refers to the physical area or environment where a species lives.
 
• **Ecological Niche:** Includes the functional role of the species in the ecosystem, encompassing behaviors, interactions, and resource use.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Niche Differentiation:**
 
 
• Avoids competition among species by assigning each a unique role and resource set.
 
• Promotes coexistence and stability within ecosystems.

questions.question: Under which Articles of the Indian Constitution are the Fundamental Rights enshrined?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 12-35**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights** are enshrined in **Part III** of the Indian Constitution and are guaranteed under **Articles 12-35**.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are a set of rights that promote the ideal of political democracy and protect the rights of individuals against the arbitrary actions of the state and other entities.
 
• These rights are justiciable, meaning they are enforceable by courts, and individuals can move the courts if these rights are violated.
 
• **Articles 12-35** broadly cover the following rights:
 
 
• Right to Equality (Articles 14-18).
 
• Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22).
 
• Right against Exploitation (Articles 23-24).
 
• Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25-28).
 
• Cultural and Educational Rights (Articles 29-30).
 
• Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).
 
 
 
• These rights ensure the protection of individual liberty and uphold the principle of equality.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Articles 12-35.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Right to Equality (Articles 14-18):**

 
 
• **Article 14:** Provides for equality before the law and equal protection of laws within the territory of India.
 
• **Article 15:** Prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
 
• **Article 16:** Ensures equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• **Article 17:** Abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• **Article 18:** Prohibits the state from conferring titles except military and academic distinctions.
 
 
 
• **Right to Freedom (Articles 19-22):**
 
 
• **Article 19:** Guarantees six freedoms, including speech, expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.
 
• **Article 20:** Provides protection in respect of conviction for offenses.
 
• **Article 21:** Ensures protection of life and personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
 
• **Article 22:** Provides protection against arrest and detention in certain cases.
 
 
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32):**
 
 
• **Article 32:** Empowers individuals to approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
 
• This article makes the judiciary the guardian and protector of Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• They are essential for the development of an individual's personality and to protect their dignity.
 
• They aim to establish equality, justice, and freedom in the country.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 32:** Known as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution, this article provides the right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
 
• **Exceptions to Fundamental Rights:** These rights are not absolute and are subject to reasonable restrictions, such as public order, security of the state, and morality.
 
• **Amendments:** Fundamental Rights can be amended, but the basic structure doctrine ensures that their essential features cannot be altered.
 
• **Suspension During Emergency:** Under Article 359, the enforcement of certain Fundamental Rights can be suspended during a national emergency except for Articles 20 and 21.

• Neeraj achieved this remarkable feat with a **throw of 88.06 meters**, which was not only his personal best at the time but also set a new **national record** in javelin throw. *Hence, the correct option is Asian Games.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Neeraj Chopra** is a distinguished Indian track and field athlete specializing in **javelin throw**.
 
• He was born on **December 24, 1997**, in **Khandra village, Haryana**.
 
• Neeraj has become a symbol of Indian sportsmanship and is celebrated for his numerous achievements, including his historic gold medal at the **Tokyo Olympics 2020**.

• **Asian U20 Championships:**

 
 
• Neeraj Chopra did participate in the **Asian U20 Championships**, where he showcased his talent as a young athlete. However, it was not the tournament where he won a gold medal in 2018.
 
 
 
• **Olympic Games:**
 
 
• Neeraj Chopra won a historic gold medal at the **Tokyo Olympics 2020**, but this event took place in **2021** due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
 
 
• **World Championships:**
 
 
• Neeraj Chopra has been a strong contender at the **World Championships**, securing a silver medal in 2022. However, he did not win a gold medal at this event in 2018.
